Axiom:
Catch-Log-Recover is the only pattern in business-logic catch blocks. First `logger.error` with Trace-Prefix and context, then recovery in ONE of two forms depending on the surrounding method's contract: - throw-style API (canon default — every new public API) → `throw new Error("[Trace-Prefix] msg", { cause })`. - Result-style API (narrow exception only, per `AX_RESULT_PUBLIC_BOUNDARY` — an existing Result-typed surface, never the default pick for new code) → `return fail(error)` (per project Result conventions; the `error` carries `{ cause }` via its own constructor).
`logger.error` records the failure with its context at detection time — this is the LDD trace (debug-level escalation lets an agent reconstruct the data path even when stacks are minified or aggregator-truncated). Recovery preserves control flow.
Both forms require both steps. Skipping `logger.error` makes the failure invisible to the trace; skipping recovery swallows it. NEVER do both (log + throw + return fail) — that re-emits and double-logs across boundaries.
